title: PEPPERPOT: DJ Freedem, Love Higher, PSYCHOMOB, samisosa B2B Samantha DaSilva
description: PEPPERPOT returns to Honey's on Thursday, October 15, from 8PM-1AM. Kicking things off on the rooftop before taking the party downstairs into the Winery, expect another night of high-energy sounds, genre-blurring selectors, and club music, well mixed. PEPPERPOT is a genre-blending dance party series inspired by the movement of music, people, and culture. Founded by Brooklyn-based artist, Samantha DaSilva, the series takes its name from Guyana's national dish. With indigenous origins and countless regional variations shaped through migration, exchange, and generations of shared tradition, pepperpot serves as a fitting metaphor for the evolution of club music itself. Coming from a mixed Indo-Guyanese, Portuguese, Caribbean, and South American background, and growing up in diverse spaces across New York, Samantha has long been drawn to the ways music travels, across borders, communities, and generations. PEPPERPOT is an extension of that perspective: a space that honors the roots of music while celebrating the many paths it has taken and the cultures that continue to shape it. It's a celebration of curiosity over categories, connection over assumptions, and a reminder that some of the most meaningful moments on a dancefloor happen when people step outside the boxes they're expected to fit into.

title: Outer Heaven presents: Timo Lee - UMA DJ
description: Hailing from the Pacific Ocean, DJ/producer Timo Lee. Now she lives in Brooklyn, play at many nightclubs including Good Room and on The Lot Radio. She is the curator for Good Bar’s vinyl sessions, label boss of Chomp! Chomp! Records and Bevy in Honolulu. Timo Lee emerged her background in Honolulu and Taipei. From early childhood, Timo has kept her ear to the speaker, fingers tapping to the rhythm. A child of the 90’s, she was weaned on rave culture’s pulsing electronic beats. As the 2000’s progressed, her tastes evolved as she embraced underground disco, house, electronica. Her love for music manifested in a remarkable way as she hosted a three-hour weekly radio show on KTUH Honolulu for eight years. During this time, Timo shared the stage with a constellation of talented DJs, including luminaries like DJ Harvey, Bonobo, James Murphy, Thomas Bullock, DJ Garth, Tiger and Woods, Daniele Baldelli, Tim Sweeney, and many others at thirtyninehotel. She also served as the club's booker for six years, actively shaping the local dance scene in Hawaii. In 2014, Timo took her talents to the bustling streets of Brooklyn, NY. Commuting between the energetic vibes of NYC and her beloved Honolulu, she curated the atmosphere at Bevy, a popular cocktail discotheque in Kaka'ako with a 100-person capacity. title: Rendezvous Grooves Open decks
description: Rendezvous Grooves returns every Thursday with Open Decks at Idle Mind Tavern. Five hours of music, five DJs, and one-hour sets built to give each artist enough time to settle in, take risks, and properly show their sound. No rushed 15-minute slots. No pressure to play a specific style. Just an open booth and a room built around discovering new selectors. Every Thursday 9PM–2AM Idle Mind Tavern 623 Manhattan Ave, Brooklyn, NY DJs interested in playing can sign up through @808.rendezvous.

title: Matthew O'Neill 'Through To Us' Album Release Preview
description: Catskills-based composer and sound artist Matthew O’Neill brings Through to Us to Ridgewood for a special live preview of his forthcoming album. Composed from field recordings, synthesizers, acoustic instruments, and sounds gathered from the landscape around his home, the record moves between composed music, improvisation, ambient sound, and something harder to name — a living conversation with the living world. For this special preview, O’Neill will be joined by Theatre of Divine Resonance and Herblore Esoterica for an evening of immersive, exploratory performance. Come for the music, stay for the strange frequencies, good company, and whatever happens in the room. Through to Us is out October 16 on Panther Mountain. Matthew O’Neill is a Catskills-based composer, songwriter, sound artist, and performer. His work moves between experimental composition, field recording, electronics, acoustic sound, and songwriting, exploring music as a form of relationship and reciprocity with land, water, memory, and the living world. He is the founder and director of Panther Mountain, a non profit music label and cultural organization.
